v.rationale: All three meet the core flow: a transactional reply insert and counter increment, then mail and database notifications sent after commit, with mentions deduplicated, matched case-insensitively and excluding the author. All suites pass. Impl-1 is the cleanest. Thread::addReply owns the transaction, mention resolution is a collection pipeline, the factory's usernames fit the mention pattern, and it has the most thorough tests, including rollback when the counter increment fails. Impl-2 is idiomatic, but probing found two real bugs. Its faker userName() factory produces dotted usernames its \w+ pattern can't match: only 15 of 30 factory users were mentionable. Its username migration also can't roll back on SQLite because the unique index isn't dropped first. Impl-3 has no bugs found and handles dotted usernames, but puts all the logic in the controller, uses plain PHP arrays instead of collections, makes user_id and reply_count mass-assignable and carries boilerplate. Because bugs weigh heavily, it ranks above impl-2.
